newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan stocks end slightly up on electronics.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan stocks end slightly up on electronics.

text.p: Taiwan share prices closed slightly higher on Tuesday, boosted by a strong electronics' sector and Monday's confidence-boosting central bank statement.
The benchmark stock index ended up 8.75 points or 0.10 percent at 8,430.62. But brokers said, however, they expected consolidation ahead.
Turnover was an active T$103.8 billion, but was only about half of the level when the market rallied in early April.
Electronic shares, which had encountered the heaviest profit-taking in recent sessions, extended Monday's rebound, surging 2.37 percent.
Motherboard giant Asustek rose by the daily seven percent limit to T$791. Computer part maker Compeg also soared to its upper limit, rising T$12 at T$186.

Brokers said the market gained support from a statement by deputy central bank governor Hsu Chia-tung on Monday that the bank, which has tried to cool the island's recent bourse fever, would like to see "appropriate" growth.
"However, recent huge net selling by both foreign and local institutional investors would continue to dampen sentiment," said HSBC James Capel analyst Stephen Wang.
Electrical and tourism shares also rose, but constructions, textiles, and transports fell.
Brokers said the market did not react to late morning news that Taiwan's March export orders and industrial output rose 5.61 percent and 10.01 percent year-on-year, respectively.
They said the consolidation should continue.
"The market now lacks bellwether shares to lead the overall upward momentum. Each leading sector recently was only strong for one day, not enough to boost momentum," Wang said.
For Wednesday, a 8,350-8,500 range was seen.
